newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts to push up, resistance at 109-08.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts to push up, resistance at 109-08.

text.p: British gilts will try to push higher on Monday but face initial resistance at 109-08, followed by a stronger cap at 109-18 to 109-21, technical analysts said.
On the downside, Friday's low of 108-14 will offer initial support, followed by a stronger prop at 108-05, the low on April 1 and the bottom of the move down from the contract high.

"Gilts will be range bound in 108-05 to 109-18 over the next week or so, but today, if anything, I'm looking for a bit of an upside probe to test the lower top at 109-08," said Howard Friend, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch here.
The market hit a daily high of 109-08 on April 11.
By 0714 GMT, the June gilt was up 3/32 at 108-22, after opening 1/32 down at 108-18.
"In the medium term I'm quite bearish, with a big resistance zone at 109-18 to 109-21," said Friend, adding the market had stalled there a number of times since March 25.
"I'm looking for consolidation under those levels with a view to breaking down eventually, but it will probe the upside first," Friend added.
Friend said if the market dropped below 108-14 during Monday but managed to close above it, it would be quite a bullish signal for Tuesday.
"But if we broke 108-05 I'd get quite bearish. But until we crack that, I don't see the whole thing breaking down just yet."
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell agreed 109-18 would hold the June gilt on the upside, before a downside breakout.
"For now, the contract remains locked in the 109-21/108-05 range, with risk retained at the 109-18 potential base neckline," DMG said in a note.
A break of that would threaten the 110-07/11 region ahead of 111-00, it added.
On the downside, a break below 108-05 would open up a move down to the 107-24 area, then 106-08 further out.
By 0736 GMT, June short sterling was up one basis point at 93.38.
DMG noted the contract was well-supported at 93.35, with resistance at 93.39 keeping it range-bound.
"An upside break would spark a push to 93.43, even 93.46," said DMG. "More likely to retreat back to 93.35."
